title: Onboarding approval lane & contract SLAs kick-off
next_steps: Jordan to send initial MSA + DPA redline bundle (tracked) by 2025-04-24
Priya to run a 1-hour pilot throughput benchmark on staging with Arcadia data patterns week of 2025-04-28
Arcadia Legal (Olivia) to provide list of non-starters in DPA by 2025-04-25
Samir to confirm procurement approval lane and PO timeline by 2025-05-02
action_items: Jordan Lee - upload pricing worksheet + seat vs committed capacity options - due 2025-04-23
Priya Menon - share benchmark runbook and preflight checklist - due 2025-04-24
Olivia Park - provide DPA redline priorities (P0/P1) - due 2025-04-25
Samir Patel - confirm internal procurement gating owners and expected PO date - due 2025-05-02
header: Date: 2025-04-21 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45 min | Attendees: Jordan, Priya (Redwood) + Samir, Lena, Marcus, Olivia (Arcadia)
transcript: [00:00] Jordan Lee: Alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving out time. Um this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the account owner for Arcadia
[00:08] Priya Menon: hi all, Priya on the call, i'll be the SE, i'll run the tech bits and the bench later
[00:12] Speaker 1: hey thanks, Samir here from procurement, we have Olivia from legal and lena from security also on the line
[00:18] Olivia Park: hey, hi all, quick note we'll be mainly reviewing DPA and SSO/KMS constraints, and i have a few non-starters already
[00:26] Marcus Reed: morning / afternoon, Marcus CTO, want to make sure the SLA and latency stuff is aligned with payments windows
[00:34] Jordan Lee: great, agenda — quick alignment on approval lane, handoff owners, pricing path, then DPA/MSA redlines, and tech preflight (bench + connectivity), any other items?
[00:42] Samir Patel: procurement timeline is the thing — we need pricing approved to get a PO to finance by first week of may, so that's kinda the urgency
[00:51] Lena Cho: security things: SOC2 attestations we need, keying model (bring your own key vs redwood KMS), and egress/data residency concerns
[01:00] Jordan Lee: noted — for SOC2 we have the attestation PDF, i'll share that, and we support customer-managed key integrations with KMS/HSM in our private offering

[01:10] Priya Menon: to set expectations: hosted api is fastest to prod, Redwood Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; private (vpc/on-prem) gives KMS in-line but has longer lead time
[01:22] Marcus Reed: rough question — for payment fraud models, we need sub 200ms p99 for single-turn chat lookups. can dedicated do that at our QPS?

[01:32] Priya Menon: yes, with the right instance sizing and batching profile we can be under 200ms p99, we'll validate in the bench. caveat: heavy batching to save cost increases latency, so we tune per-route
[01:45] Olivia Park: on the DPA, we have two non-starters: 1) indefinite retention of logs, 2) unlimited subprocessing without notice. we'll send specifics
[01:56] Jordan Lee: ok understood, we'll propose retention windows and subprocessors list. i'll mark those as P0 concerns
[02:05] Samir Patel: procurement needs to know reserved vs on-demand pricing. is there a simple delta chart?

[02:12] Jordan Lee: yes, i'll send a pricing matrix — basic hosted per-token rate, plus dedicated monthly commit tiers and a blended token+instance model. also note startup credits aren't applicable for enterprise commits
[02:25] Priya Menon: for the pilot we recommend a 2-week dedicated sandbox with scaled-down commit so you can validate throughput and fallbacks
[02:35] Lena Cho: what's the fallback policy if a model variant degrades? any SLA credits or auto-failover to cheaper models?
[02:42] Jordan Lee: we have automated fallback policies — route to compatible model variants in the same family; SLA credits are scoped in the Dedicated contract. we'll share the SLA doc
[02:52] Marcus Reed: and logging — we need audit logs at token-level for regulated transactions, does Redwood provide that granularity?
[02:59] Priya Menon: yes audit logs include request metadata and token cost breakdown at route level; full transcripts can be disabled for PII-sensitive routes
[03:10] Olivia Park: can you clarify encryption in transit and at rest with private deployment? we need to know key custody
[03:18] Jordan Lee: in Private you can plug your KMS; in Dedicated we offer optional BYOK for keys at rest and TLS for transit. i'll include a KMS integration note
[03:28] Samir Patel: one friction — finance wants a yearly commit but legal wants to keep termination window tight. typical redwood terms?
[03:36] Jordan Lee: standard commercial: annual for Dedicated with 60-day termination window for material breach; we can negotiate termination clauses but financial commit affects pricing bands
[03:46] Olivia Park: also, export controls and data residency — Arcadia processes EU payments, we need EU data residency and have to restrict egress to specified regions

[03:55] Priya Menon: we can pin regions and route by policy; private deployments enable full on-prem or VPC, which satisfies residency. hosted with region pinning also possible but audit needs may prefer private
[04:06] Marcus Reed: bench question: will you be able to mimic our traffic shape? we have spiky QPS at settlement times
[04:12] Priya Menon: yes, please share the QPS profile and modal sequence lengths; i'll create a bench config to simulate peak windows — we'll run both latency and throughput curves
[04:22] Jordan Lee: action — Priya will own bench, i will own contract coordination, olivia will own legal redlines, samir will own procurement lane mapping
[04:30] Samir Patel: procurement lane mapping — we use a two-stage approver: AEs legal sign-off then finops final approval, could take 2 weeks once pricing is final
[04:40] Jordan Lee: ok if we target sending redlines and pricing by Fri 2025-04-24, does that give you time to route?
[04:46] Samir Patel: yes, we can start routing once we have final pricing doc and the MSA redlines
[04:52] Lena Cho: security question: do you support SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning?
[04:56] Priya Menon: yes SSO/SAML and SCIM are supported; for private we can integrate with your IdP directly
[05:03] Olivia Park: a small nit — indemnity and data breach clauses, we generally need a cap tied to fees; is that negotiable?
[05:11] Jordan Lee: indemnity caps are typically negotiable for enterprise deals — i'll flag that in the MSA redline bundle
[05:18] Speaker 2: (inaudible) ...the SLA for uptime, what's the uptime number?
[05:24] Jordan Lee: for Dedicated we commit to 99.95% uptime; for hosted it's 99.9% with higher tiers available. credits are pro-rated
[05:33] Marcus Reed: on observability — do you expose per-route tracing and token cost so we can break down billing?
[05:39] Priya Menon: yes console has per-route dashboards, token breakdown, and trace IDs you can pull into your observability stack
[05:47] Samir Patel: procurement will want line items for egress fees and key-management fees, make sure those are explicit
[05:54] Jordan Lee: will do — pricing worksheet will show token, instance, egress, and KMS pass-through fees
[06:02] Olivia Park: on subprocessors — we need a fixed list and notice period for new subprocessors; can't accept open-ended language
[06:08] Jordan Lee: understood — we'll provide current subprocessor list and 30-day notice for changes as a compromise
[06:15] Lena Cho: also need to confirm retention for logs, specifically we need 90-day retention default and extended retention on request
[06:22] Jordan Lee: default 90 is reasonable, extended retention can be added for a fee or via Dedicated/private config
[06:30] Priya Menon: quick tech aside — for the bench we may use an internal cost-saving profile (intelligent batching) but will run at minimal batch to measure raw latency too
[06:40] Marcus Reed: will the bench consume any customer data? we want masked runs or synthetic data
[06:45] Priya Menon: we prefer synthetic or hashed data; we can work with you to generate a workload that mirrors your token lengths without sensitive info
[06:52] Jordan Lee: linking a doc — (shared) "MSA redline template" and "Pricing matrix v1" — we'll push to the thread after call
[07:00] Samir Patel: on approvals — our internal policy requires legal + procurement + finops signatures for any > $100k ARR, so we'll be watching that
[07:09] Jordan Lee: noted — i'll include an ARR estimate for each pricing tier to help routing
[07:17] Olivia Park: question about breach notification timing — 72 hours is a must for us
[07:22] Jordan Lee: we can commit to 72-hour notification in dedicated/private; hosted may have a different SLA but we'll default to 72 where possible
[07:30] Lena Cho: technical control: do you keep KV cache dumps? i heard 'kv cash' in an earlier doc — we need clarity
[07:36] Priya Menon: sorry yes it's KV cache — we don't persist KV caches beyond request scope by default and can disable caches for regulated routes
[07:44] Marcus Reed: any visibility into runtime kernel selection or quantization that could affect behavior? we need to reproduce issues
[07:51] Priya Menon: runtime traces include kernel version and quantization profile, we can attach those to support tickets
[07:59] Jordan Lee: ok moving toward wrap — recap: redlines + pricing by Fri 4/24; bench config share by Priya by Mon 4/28; Arcadia to send DPA priorities by 4/25
[08:10] Olivia Park: yes i'll send P0/P1 list; don't assume we accept unlimited subprocessors or indefinite log retention
[08:17] Samir Patel: procurement will start PO lane once pricing and MSA are stable — i'll confirm routing owners by 5/2
[08:24] Jordan Lee: and i'll follow up with a calendar invite for a bench run and a contract sync next week
[08:30] Speaker 1: (crosstalk) ok thanks everyone
[44:00] Jordan Lee: thank you all, we'll follow up in thread, notes and next steps will be in the email. bye
[44:08] Priya Menon: thanks — i'll schedule the bench and share the runbook
[44:12] Olivia Park: thanks, bye
[44:15] Marcus Reed: bye
[44:20] Samir Patel: thanks everyone, bye
[44:25] Lena Cho: thanks, bye
